newsitem.title: USA: SNET says enters Conn. cable TV market.
newsitem.headline: SNET says enters Conn. cable TV market.

text.p: Southern New England Telecommunications Corp. (SNET) said Tuesday it began signing up its first cable TV customers in Connecticut.
The company launched its SNET americast service, becoming the first firm to compete in the state-regulated cable TV industry.

Connecticut is one of only eight states in the U.S. that regulates cable TV on a state basis, instead of by municipality. The state is divided into 24 franchise territories, each assigned to a different cable operator.
Several of those franchise territories are served by the same corporate entity.
The state's 12 existing providers include TCI Communications Inc, Cablevision Systems Corp, Comcast Corp, and Cox Communications.
State authorities last September granted SNET the first statewide cable TV franchise in the U.S.
SNET began signing customers on Tuesday in Unionville, a suburb of Farmington, Conn. Its service offers 80 channels including local broadcast, expanded basic, premium and pay-per-view.
SNET said it will offer service to more than one third of Connecticut's 1.3 million households by the end of next year.
The company is building a $4.5 billion telephone and cable TV network throughout the state that is expected to be completed in the year 2007, a SNET spokeswoman said.
SNET americast is the cable TV unit of SNET.
Nationally, americast is the consortium of Ameritech Corp, BellSouth Corp, GTE Corp, SBC Communications, SNET and Disney TeleVentures, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Walt Disney Co.
